# Repository-backed Linux survey

Change `request.txt`, commit and push the session branch, or manually dispatch the workflow on that branch. One Ubuntu runner executes `./test.sh`, then surveys the runner user, a newly created unprivileged user, and root. `runs/linux-permissions.json` contains signal **availability only**, with the run date, kernel and architecture; it contains no identifier values. `runs/latest.log` contains sanitized test output and survey errors. Both are committed directly to the same branch; no artifacts are used. The result commit does not trigger a second run.

The `ubuntu-latest` runner is one GitHub-hosted virtual machine, not a representative physical Linux desktop or every distribution/sandbox. Runner and isolated-user results may differ because of permissions and group membership. A missing device, unsupported tool, unreadable value or placeholder is reported rather than replaced with an invented ID. Root is tested **only on the disposable runner**; the frontend does not automatically request root.

Only run tests whose stdout/stderr are safe to commit. Never print real identifiers, profiles, credentials, or API keys. Workflow setup failures before the test/survey steps remain in GitHub infrastructure logs and cannot be captured by the repository; a push conflict or disabled write permissions can also prevent saving results. If the branch moves during execution, the job fails instead of overwriting newer work. Actions and `GITHUB_TOKEN` writes must be enabled. The one-runner concurrency setting applies to this workflow, not unrelated workflows. Windows/macOS collectors do not exist yet.
